result:
I fixed project archiving so it only archives issues that were still live. The repository, service and server tests all pass (138 tests); I didn't add a test for this exact case (9 live issues plus 3 archived earlier).

**Cause:** When a project was archived with its issues, every issue in the project got a new archive date, including ones archived by hand weeks earlier. That returned 12 instead of 9. The same 12 went into the audit log ("Archived project with 12 issues") and was subtracted from the issues-used meter, which pushed the meter below the real count and sometimes below zero.

**Changes:**
- **`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`** (`archiveIssuesForProject`): now only touches issues in that project that aren't archived yet. Issues already archived keep their original archive date. The count it returns is only the newly archived issues, and that count feeds the audit-log entry and the event other parts of the app react to. The query still filters by workspace and project, so other projects aren't affected.
- **`src/server/services/usage-service.ts`**: when a project is archived, the usage counters are now recounted from the database instead of adjusted by subtracting the archived-issue count. So the issues-used meter always matches a recount of live issues. It also corrects the meter at the next project archive in any workspace where it has already drifted. Other workspaces are corrected by the periodic usage rollup job.

This doesn't repair data that's already wrong: the 3 older issues in the reported workspace still have this week's archive date. Their original dates would have to be restored some other way (for example from the audit log) before the retention sweep reaches them.
